meta.blurb: Out of breath on the stairs at forty-four, Kofi walks into a gym for the first time. His coach Ana teaches him a few basic movements, from the squat to the carry, and shows him how to add weight slowly and safely.
meta.bible: Kofi: a forty-four-year-old office worker who has never lifted weights and starts at a gym, the main character. Ana: his coach at the Riverside community gym, calm, funny and practical. Adwoa: Kofi's eight-year-old niece, quick and cheeky, who races him up the stairs. Dr Mensah: Kofi's family doctor. Tomas: runs the front desk at Riverside Gym. Mrs Okafor: a seventy-one-year-old retired teacher who started lifting at sixty-five and leads the Tuesday class. Efua: Kofi's mother, seventy. Daniel: Kofi's colleague, who joins him later. Setting: Riverside Gym, a friendly gym with free weights, a few machines and a quiet corner for beginners. Key terms: Squat, Hinge, Deadlift, Press, Row, Carry, Barbell, Dumbbell, Kettlebell, Bands, Repetition, Reps, Sets, Warm-up, Soreness, Overload, Plateau, Deload, Protein, Posture, Grip, Spotter, Machines, Technique. Voice: warm, clear and encouraging, with one simple idea in each beat. The advice is general and hedged: no single programme is the best, people differ, and nothing here is a diagnosis or a personal plan. This book is general information and is not medical advice.

beats.scene: Kofi stops halfway up an office staircase, gripping the rail and breathing hard
beats.summary: Kofi, forty-four, is out of breath on the office stairs and knows something must change.

beats.scene: Adwoa races up the stairs of a block of flats while Kofi lags behind
beats.summary: His niece Adwoa beats him easily in a race up the stairs, which is funny and also a warning.

beats.scene: A small leaflet for a beginners' hour is pinned to an office notice board
beats.summary: At work Kofi sees a leaflet for a beginners' hour at Riverside Gym and takes it home.

beats.scene: Kofi stands outside the glass door of a gym with a sports bag
beats.summary: After a week of doubt, Kofi stands outside the door of the gym and finally goes in.

beats.scene: Ana, a coach in a blue shirt, shakes hands with Kofi inside the gym
beats.summary: Ana the coach welcomes him and says that everyone in the gym started as a beginner.

beats.scene: Ana and Kofi sit at a small table with tea and a notebook
beats.summary: Ana asks what he wants from training, and Kofi says he wants stairs and shopping bags to feel easy.

beats.scene: Ana points to dumbbells, a barbell, rubber bands and a machine
beats.summary: Strength training means making muscles work against resistance, and heavy means heavy for you.

beats.scene: Kofi lifts a heavy bag of shopping out of a car boot
beats.summary: Strength helps with everyday life, such as carrying shopping, climbing stairs and getting up from a chair.

beats.scene: A drawing of a bone growing thicker beside an arm muscle
beats.summary: Muscle and bone are lost slowly with age, and research suggests lifting helps to slow this.

beats.scene: Kofi reads a health form on a clipboard at the gym desk
beats.summary: Anyone with a health condition or worrying symptoms should see a doctor before starting, so Kofi books an appointment.

beats.scene: Ana leads Kofi past rows of machines while Tomas waves from the front desk
beats.summary: Ana gives Kofi a tour of Riverside Gym, starting with the machines and the front desk.

beats.scene: A rack of dumbbells in a neat row, each marked with a number
beats.summary: Dumbbells come in pairs and in many weights, and the numbers show the weight in kilograms.

beats.scene: Ana rests a hand on a barbell loaded with round plates on a rack
beats.summary: A standard barbell weighs about twenty kilograms on its own, although lighter bars exist for beginners.

beats.scene: Kettlebells in a row on the floor beside rubber bands hanging on hooks
beats.summary: Kettlebells and rubber bands are two more kinds of resistance, and both are useful.

beats.scene: A quiet corner with mats, a mirror and a low wooden box
beats.summary: Ana shows him a quiet corner where beginners can practise without feeling watched.

beats.scene: Mrs Okafor, white-haired, lifts small dumbbells calmly beside a mat
beats.summary: Kofi sees Mrs Okafor, seventy-one, lifting weights calmly, and learns that she began at sixty-five.

beats.scene: Kofi flexes an arm in front of a gym mirror and looks unconvinced
beats.summary: Big muscles take years of hard work, so beginners will not suddenly become bulky.

beats.scene: A calendar with two days marked in blue beside a pair of dumbbells
beats.summary: Health guidelines advise muscle-strengthening activity on at least two days a week.

beats.scene: Five chalk drawings on a board: squat, bend, push, pull, carry
beats.summary: Ana says to start simple, with a few big movements that use many muscles at once.

beats.scene: Ana writes a day and time on a small card for Kofi
beats.summary: Kofi books his first lesson for Thursday evening and leaves feeling nervous and curious.

beats.scene: A whiteboard with five words written in large letters
beats.summary: The five basic movements are the squat, the hinge, the push, the pull and the carry.

beats.scene: Kofi holds nothing at all and stands with his hands by his sides
beats.summary: Technique comes before weight, so Ana begins Kofi's first lesson without any weight at all.

beats.scene: Kofi lowers himself onto a wooden box behind him and stands up again
beats.summary: The squat is just sitting down and standing up, and a box behind him makes it feel safe.

beats.scene: Chalk marks on the floor show where Kofi should place his feet
beats.summary: He stands with feet about shoulder width apart and toes turned slightly outward.

beats.scene: Ana points to Kofi's knees and feet during a squat
beats.summary: The whole foot stays on the floor, and the knees follow the direction of the toes.

beats.scene: Kofi squats with his chest up and his eyes looking straight ahead
beats.summary: Keep the chest up and the back in a strong, natural shape instead of rounded.

beats.scene: Kofi breathes in at the top of a squat and out as he rises
beats.summary: Breathe steadily through the movement and do not hold your breath for long.

beats.scene: Kofi drops quickly onto the box and Ana holds up a calming hand
beats.summary: Lowering slowly with control is better than dropping, so Kofi learns to take his time.

beats.scene: Ana films Kofi squatting with a phone and shows him the video
beats.summary: Watching a short video helps him to see his own technique and make small corrections.

beats.scene: Kofi finishes ten squats, laughing, while Ana gives him a thumbs up
beats.summary: Kofi finishes ten slow squats, feels his thighs working and discovers that he enjoyed them.

beats.scene: Ana pushes her hips back to close an imaginary car door behind her
beats.summary: The hinge means pushing the hips back and bending forward from the hips, not from the waist.

beats.scene: Kofi holds a long stick against his back while he bends forward
beats.summary: A stick along the spine helps Kofi feel whether his back stays straight as he hinges.

beats.scene: Kofi curls his back like a cat while Ana shakes her head and laughs
beats.summary: A rounded back is the most common mistake, so Ana shows him how to keep it long.

beats.scene: Kofi bends forward with soft knees and feels his thighs stretch behind
beats.summary: In a good hinge the knees stay softly bent and the muscles behind the thighs do much of the work.

beats.scene: Kofi hinges down to pick up a dumbbell from the floor, back straight
beats.summary: He practises with a light dumbbell, keeping it close and his back straight.

beats.scene: A barbell with two small plates rests on the floor on rubber blocks
beats.summary: The deadlift is a hinge with a weight, and the bar starts from the floor or from small blocks.

beats.scene: Kofi stands over the bar with his hands just outside his knees
beats.summary: Set up with the bar over the middle of the foot, a firm grip and a flat back.

beats.scene: Kofi stands tall at the top of a lift with his shoulders back
beats.summary: Finish by standing tall, without leaning back, as the hips and knees straighten together.

beats.scene: Kofi lowers the bar slowly to the floor, hips going back first
beats.summary: The weight goes down the same way it came up, under control, with the hips moving first.

beats.scene: Kofi lifts a basket of laundry at home with a straight back
beats.summary: At home, Kofi uses the same hinge to lift a laundry basket and feels pleased with himself.

beats.scene: Kofi leans against a wall and pushes himself away from it with straight arms
beats.summary: The push means pressing a weight or your own body away from you, and Kofi starts with a wall.

beats.scene: Kofi does a press-up with his hands on a bench and his body straight
beats.summary: A press-up with the hands on a high bench is easier than on the floor, and it works chest, shoulders and arms.

beats.scene: Kofi pauses mid press-up on a bench, face scrunched, while Ana smiles
beats.summary: The same exercise can be made easier or harder by changing the angle, so everyone can find a version that suits.

beats.scene: Kofi presses two light dumbbells above his head while standing tall
beats.summary: A press above the head works the shoulders, and it is done with the ribs down and no arching of the back.

beats.scene: Kofi rolls his shoulders in slow circles before pressing
beats.summary: Shoulders are flexible but easily irritated, so warm them up and stop if you feel a sharp pinch.

beats.scene: Kofi pulls a cable handle toward his chest while seated at a machine
beats.summary: The pull means drawing a weight toward you, and the seated row works the muscles of the back.

beats.scene: Kofi rows a dumbbell with one hand and one knee on a bench
beats.summary: In a dumbbell row the elbow travels back toward the hip, and the shoulder blade moves with it.

beats.scene: Kofi pulls a long bar down to his chest at a pulldown machine
beats.summary: A pulldown machine lets a beginner train the muscles used for pull-ups, with a weight he can choose.

beats.scene: A side drawing of a rounded desk worker beside a tall upright one
beats.summary: Pulling balances all the pushing we do, and strong back muscles help us to sit and stand taller.

beats.scene: Kofi sits tall at his office desk with his shoulders relaxed
beats.summary: Kofi feels his back working for the first time and notices that he sits taller at his desk.

beats.scene: Kofi stands in the gym holding a heavy dumbbell in each hand
beats.summary: The carry means walking while holding weights, and in its simplest form it is called the farmer's walk.

beats.scene: Kofi walks across the gym floor carrying a dumbbell in each hand, standing tall
beats.summary: He walks slowly and stands tall, with shoulders back and the weights hanging beside him.

beats.scene: Kofi's fingers tighten around a heavy handle and his knuckles turn pale
beats.summary: A carry tests the grip, and a stronger grip helps with jars, bags, door handles and everyday tasks.

beats.scene: Kofi carries one kettlebell in his right hand and keeps his body upright
beats.summary: In the one-handed carry, the muscles of the middle of the body work to stop the weight from pulling you sideways.

beats.scene: A diagram of the muscles around the middle of the body
beats.summary: The core is a group of muscles around the trunk that keep the body steady, and it is not only the stomach.

beats.scene: Ana stands tall beside a seated Kofi who slouches over his phone
beats.summary: No single posture is perfect, and moving often is as important as standing tall.

beats.scene: Kofi carries two shopping bags from a car to his front door
beats.summary: Carrying heavy bags evenly, one in each hand, feels easier and steadier than a single bag.

beats.scene: Kofi climbs stairs carrying two bags and rests once on a landing
beats.summary: Carrying uphill is harder, so Kofi starts light, takes his time and rests when he needs to.

beats.scene: Kofi sets two dumbbells down carefully by bending his knees
beats.summary: Put weights down by bending the knees and hinging, and keep the feet clear of the weights.

beats.scene: Kofi ticks five boxes on a whiteboard: squat, hinge, push, pull, carry
beats.summary: Kofi has now tried all five basic movements, and Ana says that they are the base of almost everything else.

beats.scene: Kofi arrives cold and rushed, coat still on, heading straight for the barbell
beats.summary: Kofi rushes in from a cold street and heads for the bar, and Ana stops him to explain the warm-up.

beats.scene: A thermometer drawing beside a heart and a muscle
beats.summary: A warm-up raises the heart rate and warms the muscles, and it is commonly advised to help you feel ready and move well.

beats.scene: Kofi pedals a stationary bike gently while watching a clock
beats.summary: Five to ten minutes of light movement, such as cycling or brisk walking, is a good start.

beats.scene: Kofi swings his legs and circles his arms and hips in the beginners' corner
beats.summary: Arm circles, leg swings and hip circles help the joints to move freely before lifting.

beats.scene: Kofi squats with an empty bar while Ana watches
beats.summary: A good warm-up includes practising the movement of the day with a very light weight.

beats.scene: Three barbells with growing numbers of plates standing side by side
beats.summary: Ramp-up sets move from a light weight to the working weight in small steps.

beats.scene: Kofi walks slowly around the gym with a towel on his shoulders
beats.summary: A short cool-down of gentle walking lets the heart rate settle.

beats.scene: Kofi sits on a mat with one leg stretched out, reaching toward his foot
beats.summary: Gentle stretching can feel good, but research on whether it prevents soreness or injury is mixed.

beats.scene: Kofi rolls a thigh on a foam roller while Ana shrugs
beats.summary: Foam rolling is popular and some people enjoy it, though the evidence for its benefits is modest.

beats.scene: Kofi pins a card to his fridge showing warm-up, workout and cool-down times
beats.summary: Kofi's routine settles into about ten minutes of warming up, forty of lifting and five of cooling down.

beats.scene: A blackboard showing the words sets and reps with small tally marks
beats.summary: A repetition is one lift, and a set is a group of repetitions done one after another.

beats.scene: Ana points to a chart of numbers from five to fifteen on the wall
beats.summary: Beginners often use about five to ten repetitions, and lighter or heavier weights can both build strength.

beats.scene: Kofi counts three groups of dots on a notepad while holding a pencil
beats.summary: Two or three sets of each movement is plenty for a beginner.

beats.scene: Kofi sits on a bench with a water bottle and a wall clock
beats.summary: Resting between sets matters, and heavier sets usually need about one to three minutes.

beats.scene: Kofi finishes a set, still holding the dumbbells, with two fingers raised
beats.summary: Stopping a set with a couple of repetitions left in reserve is a safe and useful guide.

beats.scene: Kofi finishes a set with a slight grimace but a straight back
beats.summary: The right weight feels hard by the last repetitions while the form stays good.

beats.scene: Kofi lowers a dumbbell slowly while Ana counts on her fingers
beats.summary: Lift smoothly and lower with control, without bouncing or swinging the weight.

beats.scene: Kofi breathes out as he pushes a dumbbell upward, Ana nodding beside him
beats.summary: Breathe steadily, and breathe out as you push or stand.

beats.scene: Kofi counts reps aloud with his mouth open mid-word
beats.summary: Counting aloud, or in your head, helps to keep a steady rhythm and avoid rushing.

beats.scene: Ana writes a simple session on a card with five exercises in a column
beats.summary: Ana writes Kofi's first full session: one movement from each of the five groups, two or three sets each.

beats.scene: Kofi stands at the gym door on a Monday evening holding his workout card
beats.summary: Kofi arrives for his first full workout, nervous, with his card and a new notebook in his bag.

beats.scene: Kofi lifts a light bar for the first time, his arms trembling slightly
beats.summary: The light weights feel hard and shaky, but Kofi finishes every set and feels a sense of success.

beats.scene: Kofi walks out of the gym into the evening light, tired but smiling
beats.summary: He leaves tired in a good way and wonders how he will feel tomorrow.

beats.scene: Kofi walks slowly down stairs holding the rail, wincing slightly
beats.summary: The next morning his legs are sore, and the stairs at work are a small adventure.

beats.scene: A drawing of a leg with tired muscle fibres beside a clock
beats.summary: Muscle soreness a day or two after new exercise is common, and it usually eases within a few days.

beats.scene: Ana points to a knee on a diagram and shakes her head gently
beats.summary: Sharp pain, joint pain or pain that does not go away is different from soreness, so stop and get advice.

beats.scene: Kofi walks in the park on a rest day, swinging his arms
beats.summary: Gentle movement on a rest day, such as walking, often eases soreness and helps recovery.

beats.scene: Kofi does his second workout and looks surprised at how much easier it feels
beats.summary: By the second workout the soreness is smaller, because the body adapts quickly to a new kind of work.

beats.scene: A weekly planner with three gym days separated by rest days
beats.summary: Two or three sessions a week with rest days between them is plenty for a beginner.

beats.scene: Kofi sticks the weekly plan on his fridge and shows it to Adwoa
beats.summary: Kofi puts the plan on the fridge and tells Adwoa that he is getting stronger.

beats.scene: Ana draws a staircase on the whiteboard with a small figure climbing it
beats.summary: Progressive overload means asking the body for a little more over time, so that it keeps adapting.

beats.scene: A list on the board: more weight, more reps, more sets, slower, smoother
beats.summary: More weight is only one way to progress: more reps, more sets, better form and a slower lowering all count.

beats.scene: Kofi adds small round plates onto each end of a barbell
beats.summary: Kofi learns to add weight in small steps by using the smallest plates in the gym.

beats.scene: A chart with reps from eight to ten written beside three sets
beats.summary: A simple rule: when all sets reach the top of the rep range with good form, add a little weight.

beats.scene: Kofi writes numbers in a small notebook between sets
beats.summary: A simple log of weights and reps shows progress and removes guesswork.

beats.scene: Kofi flips back through his notebook and sees the numbers rising
beats.summary: After a month the notebook shows clear progress, and it is a great encouragement.

beats.scene: Kofi lifts a dumbbell more smoothly while Ana watches and smiles
beats.summary: Early strength gains come partly from the nervous system learning the movement, before much muscle is added.

beats.scene: Kofi stares at a far too heavy loaded bar, then at Ana
beats.summary: A big jump in weight is tempting, but Kofi tries one, fails and learns to take smaller steps.

beats.scene: Kofi looks at his arms in a mirror after several months of training
beats.summary: Visible changes in muscle usually take weeks to months of regular training.

beats.scene: Kofi holds his first notebook beside his latest one, grinning
beats.summary: After two months, Kofi compares his first and latest pages and sees how far he has come.

beats.scene: Kofi unwraps a plain sandwich and a bag of crisps at his office desk
beats.summary: Kofi's usual lunch is a sandwich and crisps, and Ana says that food is the fuel for training.

beats.scene: A plate of eggs, beans, chicken and yogurt on a gym cafe table
beats.summary: Protein helps muscles to recover and grow, and most people can get it from ordinary food.

beats.scene: Ana and Kofi look at a food chart with a question mark
beats.summary: How much protein people need differs, and a dietitian can give personal advice.

beats.scene: Kofi spreads three small meals across a day on a kitchen table
beats.summary: Eating protein across the whole day matters more than a shake straight after training.

beats.scene: Kofi eats a balanced meal of rice, vegetables and fish
beats.summary: Eating enough overall supports training, and extreme dieting makes it harder.

beats.scene: Kofi fills a water bottle at a tap before heading to the gym
beats.summary: Drinking water before, during and after exercise helps you to feel and perform well.

beats.scene: A shelf of colourful supplement tubs with big promises on the labels
beats.summary: Most people do not need supplements, food comes first, and advertising claims are often exaggerated.

beats.scene: Kofi stirs a big pot of bean stew in his kitchen on a Sunday
beats.summary: Simple, cheap meals such as beans, lentils and eggs can cook ahead and cover several days.

beats.scene: Kofi chops colourful vegetables and fruit on a wooden board
beats.summary: Variety in fruit, vegetables and grains supports health, and no single food is magic.

beats.scene: Kofi and Adwoa share an ice cream on a park bench after a walk
beats.summary: No food is forbidden: Kofi enjoys a treat with Adwoa, because balance is better than strict rules.

beats.scene: Kofi yawns in a lift at work with his gym bag at his feet
beats.summary: After a week of late nights and early lifting, Kofi is tired, and Ana says that muscles adapt during rest.

beats.scene: Kofi sleeps in a dark bedroom with a clock showing the late hour
beats.summary: Most adults need about seven to nine hours of sleep, and good sleep supports training.

beats.scene: Kofi puts his phone on a shelf and turns off a bedside lamp
beats.summary: A simple evening routine, with the phone away and regular times, makes sleep easier.

beats.scene: Kofi reads a book in an armchair on a rest day, tea beside him
beats.summary: Rest days are part of the plan, and light movement such as walking is welcome.

beats.scene: Kofi at his desk with a tall pile of papers and a worried face
beats.summary: Busy work and stress also tire the body, and training can be lighter in a stressful week.

beats.scene: Kofi stands in the gym doorway looking at the bar, then at a bench
beats.summary: On very tired days, a lighter session is often wiser than skipping, but some days call for rest.

beats.scene: Kofi lies on a sofa with a blanket, a thermometer and a mug
beats.summary: If you are ill, rest and wait until you feel better, and ask a doctor if unsure.

beats.scene: Kofi adds a fourth gym day and sits flat-faced at the bench
beats.summary: More is not always better: an extra day made Kofi feel flat, not stronger.

beats.scene: A massage gun, an ice bath and a bed drawn side by side
beats.summary: Recovery gadgets have modest evidence, and the basics of sleep, food and rest come first.

beats.scene: Kofi sips tea on a Sunday morning and plans the week
beats.summary: Kofi's Sunday ritual of tea, a walk and a look at the week makes rest feel purposeful.

beats.scene: Kofi stares at a notebook page where the same numbers repeat for weeks
beats.summary: Kofi's numbers have not moved for three weeks, and he feels stuck.

beats.scene: A curve on the whiteboard that rises steeply and then flattens gently
beats.summary: Progress is fast at the start and slows later, and plateaus are a normal part of training.

beats.scene: Ana ticks a checklist of sleep, food, stress and regular sessions
beats.summary: Before changing the plan, check the basics: sleep, food, stress and whether the sessions really happen.

beats.scene: Ana films Kofi's squat again on her phone and plays it back
beats.summary: A new video shows that Kofi's form had slipped, and fixing it helps his progress.

beats.scene: Kofi adds one repetition instead of one more plate
beats.summary: When a jump feels too big, adding a single rep or using smaller plates keeps progress moving.

beats.scene: A calendar with one week coloured pale and marked easy
beats.summary: An easier week now and then, called a deload, can help the body to recover.

beats.scene: Kofi lifts very light weights in an almost empty gym
beats.summary: In his deload week Kofi lifts light, trains less and feels strange at first.

beats.scene: Kofi lifts a heavier bar than ever with Ana smiling behind him
beats.summary: After the deload week Kofi feels fresh, and his numbers move again.

beats.scene: Kofi climbs the stairs to his flat, then glances at a calendar
beats.summary: Strength shows in many ways, such as stairs, sleep, mood and energy, and not only in the numbers.

beats.scene: Kofi watches a very strong man across the gym, then checks his notebook
beats.summary: Comparing yourself with others is unhelpful, so Kofi compares himself with last month.

beats.scene: Kofi hesitates at the edge of a busy free-weight area, dumbbell in hand
beats.summary: On a busy evening Kofi hesitates at the free weights, sure that everyone is watching him.

beats.scene: People in the gym each look at their own weights, mirrors or phones
beats.summary: Most people are busy with their own workouts, and few notice anyone else.

beats.scene: Kofi wipes a bench with a towel and a spray bottle
beats.summary: Good gym manners start with wiping equipment after use.

beats.scene: Kofi puts plates back on a rack and slides a bar into its place
beats.summary: Returning weights to their racks keeps the gym safe and pleasant for the next person.

beats.scene: Kofi asks a man at the cable machine a question with a polite smile
beats.summary: It is fine to ask whether someone is using a machine and to share it between sets.

beats.scene: Kofi rests away from the bench while another lifter uses it
beats.summary: Rest away from the equipment, and keep your phone for after the set.

beats.scene: Kofi asks Tomas at the front desk how to adjust a machine seat
beats.summary: Staff and coaches are glad to help, and asking for help is a sign of good sense.

beats.scene: Mrs Okafor greets Kofi in the beginners' corner and invites him to her class
beats.summary: Kofi meets Mrs Okafor properly, and she invites him to watch her Tuesday class.

beats.scene: Kofi with headphones on and a small smile while others work quietly
beats.summary: Headphones and music help many people, and respecting personal space helps everyone.

beats.scene: Kofi says goodnight to Tomas at the door as he leaves the gym
beats.summary: Kofi greets people by name and finds that the gym has become his place.

beats.scene: Kofi sits at a chest press machine with his hands on the grips
beats.summary: Machines guide the movement along a fixed path, which makes them a good place for beginners to start.

beats.scene: Ana adjusts a pin in a weight stack beside a padded seat
beats.summary: A machine must be set to fit your body, with the seat, the handles and the weight all adjusted.

beats.scene: Kofi balances a heavy dumbbell on his shoulder and steadies himself
beats.summary: Free weights ask the body to balance and steer the load, so they train more muscles at once.

beats.scene: Scales with a machine on one side and a dumbbell on the other
beats.summary: Neither is best for everyone, and research suggests that both can build strength well.

beats.scene: Kofi holds two dumbbells beside a barbell on a rack
beats.summary: Dumbbells train each side separately, while a barbell makes it easy to add small amounts of weight.

beats.scene: Ana holds a kettlebell by the handle in the beginners' corner
beats.summary: A kettlebell is useful for goblet squats and carries, and swings are better learned with a coach.

beats.scene: Kofi pulls a long rubber band tight with both hands
beats.summary: Rubber bands are light and cheap, and the more they stretch, the harder they pull.

beats.scene: Kofi pulls a cable handle across his chest at a tall machine
beats.summary: A cable machine gives smooth, steady resistance and can be used for rows, pulldowns and many other moves.

beats.scene: Kofi squats and does a press-up on a mat without any equipment
beats.summary: Body weight alone is a complete and free way to train, and it can be made harder or easier.

beats.scene: Kofi writes a Friday session in his notebook mixing machines and free weights
beats.summary: The best exercise is the one that you will actually do, so Kofi chooses a mix that he enjoys.

beats.scene: A rainy gym door with a notice that says closed for repairs
beats.summary: Riverside Gym closes for a week of repairs, and Kofi wonders if he can train at home.

beats.scene: Kofi pushes a sofa aside and unrolls a mat in his living room
beats.summary: A small clear space, a mat and sensible shoes are all that a home workout needs to start.

beats.scene: Kofi squats down to a kitchen chair and stands up again
beats.summary: A sturdy chair works like the box, and a bodyweight squat to a chair is a good start.

beats.scene: Kofi squats with a backpack full of books held against his chest
beats.summary: A backpack filled with books can add weight to a squat or a hinge, and it can be loaded a little at a time.

beats.scene: Kofi does press-ups with his hands on a kitchen counter
beats.summary: Press-ups can be done at a wall, a counter or the floor, depending on strength.

beats.scene: A rubber band looped over a door handle with Kofi pulling it
beats.summary: A band fixed to a door anchor allows rows and pulls, if the band and the door are secure.

beats.scene: Kofi holds two milk jugs full of water like dumbbells
beats.summary: Bottles of water make cheap weights, because a litre weighs about one kilogram.

beats.scene: Kofi steps up onto a park bench and carries two shopping bags
beats.summary: Step-ups on a bench and carries with heavy bags are good outdoor exercises.

That weekend, his eight-year-old niece Adwoa challenges him to a race up the stairs of his block of flats. She wins easily, and she waits at the top, giggling, while he catches his breath.
On the office notice board, Kofi notices a leaflet for a beginners' hour at Riverside Gym. He reads it twice, folds it carefully and puts it in his pocket.
A week later, Kofi stands outside the glass door of the gym with a sports bag in his hand. Inside, people are lifting heavy things, and he is sure that he does not belong there.
A coach in a blue shirt walks over and shakes his hand. Her name is Ana, and she says that everybody in the gym started as a beginner.
Over a cup of tea, Ana asks what Kofi wants from training. He thinks for a moment and says that he would like stairs and shopping bags to feel easy again.
Ana points to the dumbbells, the barbell, the rubber bands and the machines. Strength training, she explains, means making muscles work against resistance, and heavy simply means heavy for you.
Strength is useful far beyond the gym, says Ana. It helps you to carry shopping, climb stairs, get up from a chair and play with children.
People slowly lose muscle as they age if they do not use it, and bones can become thinner as well. Research suggests that strength training helps to slow both changes.
Ana gives Kofi a health form to fill in at the desk. She says anyone with a health condition or worrying symptoms should see a doctor first, so Kofi promises to book a visit with Dr Mensah.
Ana walks Kofi past rows of machines and a wall of mirrors. Behind the front desk, a young man called Tomas waves and gives him a thumbs up.
Dumbbells come in pairs, each one marked with its weight in kilograms. Ana lets Kofi pick up a few of them so that he can feel how different they are.
The barbell on the rack is a long metal bar with round plates on each end. By itself it weighs about twenty kilograms, although lighter bars are made for beginners.
On the floor, a line of kettlebells stands beside rubber bands hanging from hooks. Ana says that each of these is simply another way to make a muscle work.
At the back of the gym, Ana shows Kofi a quiet corner with mats, a mirror and a low wooden box. This is where beginners practise, and nobody is allowed to stare.
Kofi notices Mrs Okafor, who is seventy-one, lifting small dumbbells with a calm face. Ana tells him that Mrs Okafor started lifting at sixty-five, and that she has never looked back.
Kofi flexes an arm in the mirror and looks unconvinced. Ana laughs and explains that big muscles take years of hard work, so he will not wake up bulky.
Health guidelines advise adults to do muscle-strengthening activity on at least two days a week. Ana says that this is a sensible target, and that it is much easier than it sounds.

On the whiteboard, Ana draws five small figures: one squatting, one bending, one pushing, one pulling and one walking. She says that beginners should start with a few big movements, not with a hundred different exercises.
